section_summary: This section contains World Federation of Trade Unions material on a confrontation in Korea, followed by reports on women in Japanese labor federations and the proposed constitution of an educational personnel union. Later documents cover union elections and democracy, farmers’ organizations, control associations, and political factions in trade unions. Several SCAP press releases also contain unrelated news briefs.

subfiles.title: W.F.T.U. delegation account of a factory incident in Korea
subfiles.from: World Federation of Trade Unions delegation
subfiles.about: The delegation describes intimidation and assaults during a Korean factory visit and demands protection and remedies.
subfiles.summary: After factory management rejected its proposed inspection arrangements, the delegation witnessed assaults on two Korean trade unionists and an armed police presence. It ended the visit and demanded the release and protection of those arrested, action against the factory managers, and guarantees of free union organization.

subfiles.title: General Council resolution on the preliminary report of the delegation to Japan and Korea
subfiles.about: The council orders publication and circulation of the delegation's preliminary and final reports.
subfiles.summary: Orders publication of the preliminary report and preparation of a final report; calls for study of Korean trade unions.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of report on women in major labor federations
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP report on women's organization, membership, and activities in Japanese labor federations.
subfiles.summary: Forwards five copies of the July 30 report on women in major labor federations.

subfiles.title: Organization, Membership, and Activities of Women in Major Labor Federations
subfiles.from: Public Opinion and Sociological Research Unit, SCAP Civil Information and Education Section
subfiles.about: Surveys women's membership, leadership, education, and employment issues in major Japanese labor federations.
subfiles.summary: The report estimates that women made up about one quarter of organized Japanese workers at the end of 1946. It examines women's sections in industrial, communications, textile, and railway unions, including their representation, education programs, wage demands, and workplace conditions. Appendices provide membership figures and organizational charts; the final pages list sources and interviewees.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of report on the National Educational Personnel Labor Union
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP translation concerning a proposed educational personnel labor union.
subfiles.summary: Forwards five copies of the April 1946 report under separate cover.

subfiles.title: The National Educational Personnel Labor Union: Declaration of the Founders, with a Draft of the Constitution
subfiles.from: Education Research Unit, SCAP Civil Information and Education Section
subfiles.about: Translates the union founders' declaration and proposed constitution.
subfiles.summary: The introductory comment describes the union as still in preparation and identifies two organizers from the Ministry of Education Personnel Labor Union. The founders call for educational autonomy, improved working conditions, higher social standing, and democratization. The draft constitution sets out membership, objectives, governing bodies, elections, finances, and rules for joining or leaving.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of announcement on speeches by SCAP labor officials
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a press announcement urging greater rank-and-file participation in Japanese unions.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the December 3 press release on democratic union leadership.

subfiles.title: Japanese trade union leaders must decide who controls policies
subfiles.from: Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP labor officials' call for member control of union policy.
subfiles.summary: Richard Deverall and Betty Wilson urge regular meetings, secret ballots, and member financing of unions. The release also includes unrelated military, sports, court, and shipping notices.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of James S. Killen's statement on Railroad Workers' Union elections
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards Killen's statement on railroad union elections and national contract negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the December 10 press release praising the railroad union's executive committee election.

subfiles.title: Far East Command press release of December 10, 1947
subfiles.from: Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Contains James S. Killen's assessment of railroad union elections alongside other news briefs.
subfiles.summary: Killen praises the Railroad Workers' Union election as evidence of member participation and support for national contract negotiations. The same release carries notices on military transport and appointments, abolition of the Home Ministry, relief parcels, and Fukui rice deliveries.

subfiles.title: SANACC 356/1: Policy for Democratization of Japanese Farmers' Unions and Cooperatives
subfiles.about: Explains the U.S. policy paper's origin and its differences from Japan's new cooperative law.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum explains why the United States submitted a farmers' organizations policy to the Far Eastern Commission after New Zealand proposed one. It compares SANACC 356/1 with Japan's Agricultural Cooperative Association law, emphasizing coverage of farmers' unions and judicial review of penalties.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of directive on control associations
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAPIN 1860 defining control associations and ordering prefectural lists.
subfiles.summary: Forwards SCAP's February 16 directive on identifying and eliminating control associations.

subfiles.title: Interpretation and Implementation of Policy Concerning the Elimination of Control Associations
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Defines control associations and orders their identification for review and possible dissolution.
subfiles.summary: Defines control associations by compulsory membership or trade rules and by control of distribution, sales, or credit. Orders prefectural governors to list such bodies within 60 days for SCAP review and subsequent action.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of materials on fraction activities in trade unions
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a press statement and pamphlet on racketeering and political factions in trade unions.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Deverall's statement and The Struggle for Trade Union Democracy.

subfiles.title: Fraction Activities in Trade Unions
subfiles.from: Richard Deverall, SCAP Labor Education Branch
subfiles.about: Explains how secret factions can manipulate unions and announces educational materials for members.
subfiles.summary: Deverall describes caucuses, intimidation, and coordinated political cells as threats to member control. He promotes a revised pamphlet and filmstrip while urging unions themselves to address factional activity.

subfiles.title: The Struggle for Trade Union Democracy
subfiles.about: Introduces threats to democratic unions from labor racketeers and political factions.
subfiles.summary: The pamphlet argues that union democracy depends on continuing member participation and education. Its opening examples describe secret caucuses, intimidation, financial exploitation, and employer deals by union bosses. It then introduces political factions that seek to steer unions toward party goals.
